bugs.name: Admin repository Updated and Size sorts omit their active indicators
bugs.summary: Updated and Size sorting reorders administrator repository rows without showing an active sort direction in the corresponding column header.
bugs.expected: The active repository sort and direction should be visible in the column header.
bugs.actual: Updated and Size sorting reorders administrator repository rows without showing an active sort direction in the corresponding column header.
reproSteps: As administrator, open Admin > Repositories after at least two repositories exist.
Choose Recently updated and Least recently updated; inspect the Updated header.
Choose Smallest size and Largest size; inspect the Size header.
Compare with a sort such as Most stars that shows its active arrow.

bugs.name: Admin Alphabetically sort groups repositories by owner before name
bugs.summary: The administrator repository inventory sorts Alphabetically by owner first, leaving repository names out of global alphabetical order.
bugs.expected: Alphabetical sorting should order all repositories by repository name.
bugs.actual: The administrator repository inventory sorts Alphabetically by owner first, leaving repository names out of global alphabetical order.
reproSteps: Create disposable repositories under two different owners with names whose global alphabetical order differs from owner order.
As administrator, open Admin > Repositories and select Sort > Alphabetically.
Compare the visible Name column with a global alphabetical order of repository names.

bugs.name: Unknown organization user actions return a 500 error
bugs.summary: Adding or blocking a nonexistent organization user returns an internal server error instead of a validation message.
bugs.expected: Organization member and block forms should reject an unknown username without a server error.
bugs.actual: Submitting an unknown user from Add member or Blocked users navigates to an HTTP 500 error page.
reproSteps: Create a disposable organization as its owner.
From Members, submit a nonexistent username in Add member without selecting a suggestion; observe HTTP 500.
From Settings > Blocked users, submit a nonexistent username in Block; observe HTTP 500.

bugs.name: Wiki read permission description uses incorrect possessive
bugs.summary: The team permission description uses “it’s” where the possessive “its” is needed.
bugs.expected: The Wiki read permission should describe “its history.”
bugs.actual: The description reads “Read the integrated wiki and it’s history.”
reproSteps: Create or open a disposable organization and choose Teams > New team.
Find the Wiki row in the custom permissions table.
Read the description of Read permission.

bugs.name: Watching list includes repositories after they are unwatched
bugs.summary: Unwatching a repository updates its watch state and watcher list, but it remains listed under Notifications → Watching even after reload. Reported variant (mo-30m-forgejo-10): The private repository remains in Notifications > Watching after Unwatch changes its header to Watch with zero watchers; the result persists after a full page refresh. Count this as the same reference rather than a separate bug.
bugs.expected: The Watching page lists only repositories the user currently watches and removes field-notes after Unwatch.
bugs.actual: field-notes remains in the Watching list despite the repository showing Watch, 0 watchers, and an empty watcher list. Reproduced twice, including fresh reloads of both pages.
reproSteps: Sign in as momentic-admin. Open /momentic-admin/field-notes, which is initially watched.
Open the Watching dropdown and click Unwatch.
Reload the repository page and confirm the control reads Watch and the count is 0 watchers.
Click 0 watchers and confirm 'No one is watching this repo.'
Open /notifications/watching and reload.
Reported variant (mo-30m-forgejo-10): Using the authorized signed-in momentic-admin session, open /notifications. No credential environment variables were used.
Reported variant (mo-30m-forgejo-10): Create a new private repository named momentic-watch-unwatch-9f3c2a under momentic-admin and select Initialize repository to create its README.
Reported variant (mo-30m-forgejo-10): On the repository page, confirm the header shows Watching with a count of 1.
Reported variant (mo-30m-forgejo-10): Use the notifications bell, open Subscriptions, select Watching, and search for momentic-watch-unwatch-9f3c2a. Confirm it appears in the results.
Reported variant (mo-30m-forgejo-10): Return to momentic-admin/momentic-watch-unwatch-9f3c2a, open the repository Watching dropdown, and click Unwatch.
Reported variant (mo-30m-forgejo-10): Confirm the repository header changes to Watch with a count of 0.

Reported variant (mo-30m-forgejo-10): Use the notifications bell, open Subscriptions > Watching, and search for momentic-watch-unwatch-9f3c2a again. The result remains visible at /notifications/watching?q=momentic-watch-unwatch-9f3c2a&sort=recentupdate.
Reported variant (mo-30m-forgejo-10): Refresh the filtered Watching page and wait for it to settle. The repository remains listed.

reviewedVariants.name: Repository remains in Notifications > Watching after unwatching
reviewedVariants.summary: The private repository remains in Notifications > Watching after Unwatch changes its header to Watch with zero watchers; the result persists after a full page refresh.
reviewedVariants.expected: After unwatching the repository, it should no longer appear in the Watching list.
reviewedVariants.actual: The repository header changed from Watching with a count of 1 to Watch with a count of 0, but searching for its exact name in Notifications > Watching still returned it. The result remained after refreshing the page and waiting for it to settle.
reproSteps: Using the authorized signed-in momentic-admin session, open /notifications. No credential environment variables were used.
Create a new private repository named momentic-watch-unwatch-9f3c2a under momentic-admin and select Initialize repository to create its README.
On the repository page, confirm the header shows Watching with a count of 1.
Use the notifications bell, open Subscriptions, select Watching, and search for momentic-watch-unwatch-9f3c2a. Confirm it appears in the results.
Return to momentic-admin/momentic-watch-unwatch-9f3c2a, open the repository Watching dropdown, and click Unwatch.
Confirm the repository header changes to Watch with a count of 0.

Use the notifications bell, open Subscriptions > Watching, and search for momentic-watch-unwatch-9f3c2a again. The result remains visible at /notifications/watching?q=momentic-watch-unwatch-9f3c2a&sort=recentupdate.
Refresh the filtered Watching page and wait for it to settle. The repository remains listed.

bugs.name: Dashboard repository filter options are clipped off-screen on a mobile viewport
bugs.summary: At 390×844, opening the dashboard repository filter places the Archived and Private labels outside the viewport; they appear only after horizontally scrolling the dashboard.
bugs.expected: When the repository filter is opened at 390×844, the Archived and Private option labels should be visible within the viewport so the user can identify them.
bugs.actual: The menu opens past the right edge. Only the left-side checkboxes and partial icons are visible; neither option label is in the viewport. Horizontal scrolling reveals both labels only by shifting the dashboard content.
reproSteps: Set the browser viewport to 390×844 CSS pixels.
Load the supplied signed-in momentic-admin admin session; do not change authentication details.
Navigate to /.
In the repository panel, click the filter button beside the repository search field.
Observe that the Archived and Private labels are beyond the viewport's right edge; only checkboxes and partial icons are visible.

reviewedVariants.name: Repository sidebar filter menu clips option labels offscreen on mobile
reviewedVariants.summary: The repository filter popover reproducibly extends beyond the right edge at 390×844, hiding the Archived and Private labels; opening it and waiting does not reposition it.
reviewedVariants.expected: At 390×844, opening the repository filter menu should keep the Archived and Private options and their labels readable in the viewport so the user can identify a filter.
reviewedVariants.actual: The menu opens at the far right edge and only its checkboxes and icons are visible; the Archived and Private labels are clipped offscreen. This remains after waiting. Horizontal panning can reveal the labels, but shifts the dashboard content sideways. Selecting Archived after revealing it filtered the list, confirming the observed issue is the menu layout rather than a failed filter action.
reproSteps: Use a 390×844 CSS-pixel viewport and start signed in as momentic-admin using the supplied authenticated session; do not change authentication details.
Navigate to /. No fixture setup is required.
In the dashboard repository sidebar, click the funnel button next to the repository search field.

Observe the open menu: its checkboxes and icons are in view, while the Archived and Private labels extend beyond the right viewport edge; wait at least five seconds to confirm the menu remains clipped.

matchingGuidance.acceptanceScope: Accepted as a valid reference by user instruction; source prerequisites and remaining evidence gaps are retained below.
prerequisites: 390px viewport, dropdown opens to right of right-edge anchor.

bugs.name: Mobile Authentication sources header truncates and hides total
bugs.summary: At 390×844, the Authentication sources header remains truncated beside the Add button and does not show its Total count after the page settles.
bugs.expected: At 390×844, the Authentication sources heading and its displayed total remain readable.
bugs.actual: The header displays “Manage authentication sour…” beside Add authentication source, with no “Total: 0.” The table shows “No results found.”
reproSteps: Set the viewport to 390×844 and use the preconfigured authenticated admin session (admin role).
Navigate to /admin.
Expand Identity & access in the admin sidebar.
Select Authentication sources; the browser reaches /admin/auths.
Without activating Add authentication source, inspect the list header. It remains truncated and omits the total after the page has settled.

matchingGuidance.acceptanceScope: Accepted as a valid reference by user instruction; source prerequisites and remaining evidence gaps are retained below.
prerequisites: 390px viewport and localized English heading/action widths.

bugs.name: Contribution calendar day opens empty dashboard and profile feeds
bugs.summary: Clicking a contribution calendar cell with a nonzero count opens an empty date-filtered activity feed on both Dashboard and profile Public activity, while unfiltered activity from that displayed day is present.
bugs.expected: Clicking a day with recorded contributions filters the activity feed to that day's contributions.
bugs.actual: For Oct 8, 2026 in the browser's PDT display, hovered contribution cells show nonzero counts (73, then 93 as testing progressed). Clicking the dashboard cell navigates to /?date=2026-10-08 and shows No activity. Clicking the profile cell navigates to /momentic-admin?tab=activity&date=2026-10-08 and empties its feed. Both unfiltered feeds contain that day's activity. Reproduced multiple times.
reproSteps: Sign in and open Dashboard (/) with activity and contribution-calendar entries present.
Hover the latest colored day and note its nonzero contribution count and displayed date (tested Oct 8, 2026).
Click that cell. Observe /?date=2026-10-08 and No activity.
Return to / and verify the populated activity feed has timestamps on the displayed day.
Open the profile's Public activity tab (/momentic-admin?tab=activity), hover and click the same nonzero calendar day.
Observe the profile date-filtered URL and empty activity feed; removing the date filter restores the entries.

matchingGuidance.acceptanceScope: Accepted as a valid reference by user instruction; source prerequisites and remaining evidence gaps are retained below.
prerequisites: Browser and server day boundaries or contribution/feed inclusion rules differ.
